tolerance to the analgesia produced by morphine in the hot plate test is a function of the testing cylinder, heat, and the combination of both factors, and that the testing cylinder is an important factor.
the hot plate method of testing for analgesia, as well as the cylinder, contributes significantly to the development of morphine tolerance.

the development of tolerance in rats to the analgesia induced by morphine.
the effects of heat and the testing cylinder on tolerance development in the hot plate.
the development of tolerance in morphine-treated rats using the hot plate method of testing.

both the heated plate and the testing cylinder are important factors in producing tolerance in this method, the combination of both being most effective in the development of tolerance.
tolerance to morphine is a function of both the heat and the testing cylinder and that the combined effect of heat and cylinder is the most potent in producing tolerance.
tolerance to morphine developed in all cases, irrespective of whether the testing cylinder was used, whether heat was a factor, and whether animals were tested on a daily or weekly schedule.

tolerance to morphine is a function of the testing procedure, the testing procedure being a combination of heat and a testing cylinder.
the development of tolerance in rats to morphine is dependent on the combined effect of both heat and the testing cylinder.

the testing cylinder should be employed in the hot plate technique, and that the testing cylinder is not only an aid in the development of tolerance but is also an important factor itself.
